Sam (Sales): @Tiffany quick heads-up — ACME's vendor risk team wants concrete answers for the encryption + KMS section of the SIG. They asked specifically about BYOK, HSM support, key rotation, and audit trail. I said I'd get a concise set of bullets by EOD.
Tiffany (Security): Got it. I'll draft a short, customer-friendly response. High-level first: at-rest = AES-256-GCM envelope encryption; in-transit = TLS 1.3 with modern ciphers.
Sam (Sales): Perfect. They also asked whether we allow customer-managed keys (BYOK) and if we can integrate with their HSM.
Tiffany (Security): Yes — we support three modes: hosted keys (Redwood-managed KMS), customer-managed cloud KMS (BYOK — e.g., AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault), and on-prem/HSM via PKCS#11 or CloudHSM for private deployments.
Priya (SE): To be explicit for the questionnaire: we use envelope encryption by default. Root CMKs never touch application storage — only used to wrap DEKs. That makes exporting datasets safe.
Tiffany (Security): Add: when BYOK is enabled we never persist plaintext customer CMKs. We store only the key reference/ARN and use the KMS API for cryptographic operations. For HSM-backed keys, we support FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM appliances) depending on deployment.
Sam (Sales): How about rotation? They want a rotation policy and whether rotation causes downtime or re-encryption.
Tiffany (Security): Rotation model: DEKs rotate independently per-customer; CMK rotation is supported via KMS-native rotation or customer-driven rotation. Re-encryption: we use envelope encryption – rotating the wrapping key (CMK) does not require immediate re-encryption of all data; new DEKs are wrapped with the new CMK. We can also offer a one-time rewrap job if customer requests full re-encryption (scheduleable, can be run as POC). Recommended default: CMK rotation 90 days for high-sensitivity, 365 days standard.
Priya (SE): Example snippet customers like to see (how to enable BYOK in config):
```yaml
redwood:
  encryption:
    mode: BYOK
    provider: aws
    cmk_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
    rotation: auto
    rotation_window_days: 90
```
Tiffany (Security): Auditability: all KMS operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey) are logged to the customer audit stream. On hosted deployments we stream KMS events to the customer's Syslog/S3/SIEM integration. Private deployments can integrate with customer SIEM directly.
Sam (Sales): They asked about key compromise procedures and SLAs.
Tiffany (Security): If compromise suspected: rotate CMK immediately, optionally trigger rewrap job, and provide full audit trail and timeline. We have runbooks for key compromise and can support incident calls. SLA for key operations: we expose health metrics and SLOs per plan — Dedicated/Private customers can get contractual availability for key APIs.
Priya (SE): Quick CLI example for granting Redwood service permission to use a customer CMK (AWS):
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id $CMK_ARN --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/service --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```
Tiffany (Security): Security posture note: keys never leave their KMS/HSM boundary. For on-prem HSM, the private key material remains in HSM (PKCS#11) and is only referenced by key handles. We support HSM attestation for high-compliance customers.
DevOps Bot: Ticket #4529 created to track ACME BYOK POC and docs deliverable, ETA 2 business days.
Sam (Sales): Thanks team — I'll send this condensed answer back to ACME and propose a 30-min security call with @Tiffany and @Priya for the POC. If you want any edits to the bullets, call them out here. :thumbsup:
Tiffany (Security): Tiny tweak: mention default cipher suites (AES-256-GCM) and endorsement of TLS 1.3 explicitly. Then fine.
Priya (SE): I'll add a short appendix with the rewrap job steps and estimated runtime for N TB.
Sam (Sales): Awesome — sending now.
